title: Oslo restricts cars in the city centre and records no pedestrian or cyclist deaths
context: Oslo adopted a Vision Zero goal for traffic deaths.
decision_made: Remove regular street parking and close the city centre to through traffic, lower speed limits, add traffic calming near schools and expand bike lanes.
action_taken: The centre restriction took effect in early 2019 and initially drew resident backlash.
observed_outcome: The city reported zero pedestrian and cyclist deaths in 2019 and again in 2023. Overall there was one traffic death in 2019, down from five in 2018.
observation_period: 1 year, with a repeat result in 2023
lessons: Combining speed reduction, street design and restrictions can cut deaths quickly, though one year of data is noisy for rare events.
limitations: Some sources wrongly claim zero road deaths overall. Serious injuries were not eliminated, and the figures are from the city itself. Several sources are advocacy or trade coverage.

claims.claim_text: Oslo removed regular street parking in the city centre and closed it to through traffic from early 2019.
Oslo and Helsinki recorded zero pedestrian and cyclist deaths in 2019.
